hypotheses.justification: Neither the statement nor the proof uses it. Everything in the statement is defined for arbitrary modulus: `ZMod.commRing (n)` and `ZMod.charP (n) : CharP (ZMod n) n` hold for every `n` (Mathlib/Data/ZMod/Defs.lean line 172, Basic.lean line 111), so `ZMod.castHom (dvd_mul_right N ℓ) (ZMod N)` is available without `NeZero`; `ZMod.unitsMap` (Data/ZMod/Units.lean line 26), `Subgroup.comap`, `CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma0` (defined for all `N`, CongruenceSubgroups.lean line 80) and `CohCarrier.GammaH` (Definitions/Def_CohCarrier_Level.lean line 133, built from the unconditional `gamma0Units`/`Gamma0Map`) need no `NeZero` either. The proof itself only calls `mem_GammaH_iff`, `Gamma0_mem`, `Units.ext` and `map_intCast`; the `NeZero` arguments never occur in it. The degenerate case `N = 0` is harmless because `ZMod 0 = ℤ` and `castHom (dvd_mul_right 0 ℓ) (ZMod 0)` is `Int.cast` into `ℤ`, i.e. the identity on integers (this is exactly what `hcast` proves, via `map_intCast`); moreover `GammaH 0 H' ≤ Gamma0 0`, so `GammaH 0 H' ⊓ Gamma0 (0*ℓ) = GammaH 0 H' = GammaH 0 (H'.comap id)`. The same `hcast`-based argument used in the proof transfers membership in `Gamma0 (N*ℓ)` to `Gamma0 N` and identifies `unitsMap (gamma0Units (N*ℓ) …)` with `gamma0Units N …` by comparing values `castHom ((γ 1 1 : ZMod (N*ℓ))) = (γ 1 1 : ZMod N)`, all unconditionally. Can be deleted together with `[NeZero (N * ℓ)]`.

Unused in the statement and the proof, and the identity stays true when `N * ℓ = 0` (i.e. `N = 0` or `ℓ = 0`). All structures involved are total: `ZMod (N*ℓ)` with `ZMod.commRing`/`ZMod.charP` instances exists for every `n`, `ZMod.unitsMap` and `CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma0`/`Gamma0Map` are unconditional, and `ZMod.castHom (dvd_mul_right N ℓ) (ZMod N)` only needs `CharP (ZMod N) N`, which is available unconditionally. The proof never invokes `NeZero`; the only arithmetic input is `hcast : ∀ z : ℤ, castHom ((z : ZMod (N*ℓ))) = (z : ZMod N)`, which is `map_intCast`. That suffices in the junk case `ℓ = 0`: `ZMod (N*0) = ZMod 0 = ℤ`, so `γ ∈ Gamma0 (N*0)` means `(γ 1 0 : ℤ) = 0`, whence `(γ 1 0 : ZMod N) = 0`, and the unit condition matches because both sides have value `(γ 1 1 : ZMod N)` (for the right-hand side the value is `castHom ((γ 1 1 : ℤ))`). In the case `N = 0` both moduli are `0` and `unitsMap` is the identity, so both sides equal `GammaH 0 H'`. Can be deleted together with `[NeZero N]`.
